_note: The full Elias Ward encounter in Interview Room A (owner playtest 2026-11-04): introduction, a full history taken from Elias and, where he cannot answer, from his 1:1 sitter and the transfer packet, a physical and catatonia examination the psychiatrist performs on screen, and verbal orders given at the bedside that are logged to the EHR. Every patient fact, finding, result, verdict and outcome below is fictional. Approved by the owner (physician) on 2026-11-05 as written, including the four review-sheet answers left as drafted (rising vitals after haloperidol, lorazepam 'as per protocol' with no dose shown, Elias's 'Thank you' after lorazepam, Tom Adler as mental health technician); see docs/clinical_review_log.md. It changes no treatment effect in ClinicalRules. Elias does not speak until the lorazepam reassessment: his non-responses are shown by his model (stillness, fixed gaze), not narrated. The 'shown' text is the on-screen transcript caption only and is never voiced. Line ids are stable: never reuse an id for different wording.
source: Original writing for The Forensic Ward. Catatonia examination steps are original summaries of the signs screened by the Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale (Bush G, Fink M, Petrides G, Dowling F, Francis A. Catatonia. I. Rating scale and standardized examination. Acta Psychiatr Scand 1996;93:129-136); no scale text is reproduced. Scene structure follows docs/design/screenplays/ForensicWard_Five_Chapter_Screenplay/chapters/CH1_ELIAS_WARD_COMPLETE_SOURCE_DRAFT.md Scenes 6-8.

informant.name: Tom Adler
informant.intro: Seated by the door on a 1:1 observation since Elias arrived at 01:40. Has the transfer packet and the nursing flowsheet on a clipboard.

steps.label: Introduce yourself to Elias
steps.player: Good morning, Mr. Ward. I'm one of the psychiatrists here at Ashcroft. Is it all right if I sit down with you for a while?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response. His eyes stay on a point on the far wall.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Morning, Doctor. I'm Tom, I'm on his one-to-one. He's been like this since he came up from admissions at twenty to two.

steps.label: Tell Elias what will happen
steps.player: You don't have to answer anything right away, Elias. I'll ask some questions, and Tom will help me with what he knows. Before I examine you I'll tell you each step first.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response. He has not blinked while you were speaking.

steps.label: Ask about pain (nod or squeeze my hand)
steps.player: Elias, are you in any pain? If it's hard to talk, you can nod, or squeeze my hand.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No nod. His hand stays limp in yours and does not squeeze.

steps.label: Ask when this started
steps.player: Elias, when did you stop feeling like talking? ... Tom, what does the packet say about when this started?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Jail medical wrote that he was withdrawn and staying in his cell for about a week. Then he stopped talking altogether, four days before the transfer. That's from the packet. Nobody here has seen him any other way.

steps.label: Ask about food and fluids
steps.player: Elias, have you been able to eat or drink anything today? ... Tom, how much has he taken?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: A few sips of water at breakfast, when I held the cup to his lips. Then he just held it in his mouth. Nothing to eat since he got here. Night staff charted about a quarter of a cup overnight.

steps.label: Ask about urine and bowels
steps.player: Tom, has he passed urine since he arrived? Any bowel movement?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: No urine charted since he arrived. The transport note says he last went yesterday afternoon at the jail. No bowel movement on our chart at all.

steps.label: Ask about sleep and the night
steps.player: Tom, how was he overnight? Did he sleep?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Hard to say. He lay on top of the covers in the same position from about three until they got him up at seven. Eyes open most of the times I checked. He didn't turn over once.

steps.label: Ask about medications given
steps.player: Tom, what medication has he had, here or at the jail? Anything in the last two weeks?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Nothing since he's been here. The jail medication record shows haloperidol injections twice, six days and five days before transfer, for agitation. Five milligrams each time, it says. Nothing regular after that. No lorazepam.

steps.label: Ask about allergies
steps.player: Elias, are you allergic to any medicines? ... Tom, any allergies recorded?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: No known drug allergies, on both the jail record and our admission sheet.

steps.label: Ask about past psychiatric history
steps.player: Elias, have you been in hospital for your mental health before? ... Tom, does the packet mention it?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: One admission when he was twenty-four, for psychosis. Discharged on an antipsychotic, and the note says he stopped it within a few months. Nothing about an episode like this one.

steps.label: Ask about medical history
steps.player: Tom, any medical problems? Seizures, head injury, anything he's treated for?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Nothing recorded. No seizures or head injury on the jail intake form. They didn't do any blood tests that I can see.

steps.label: Ask about alcohol and drugs
steps.player: Elias, do you drink, or use any drugs? ... Tom, what's on the intake form?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Daily cannabis before his arrest, he told them. Alcohol at weekends. His urine screen at jail intake was positive for cannabis only. That was six weeks ago, and he's been inside since.

steps.label: Ask about family history and contacts
steps.player: Tom, is there any family history in the packet? Who's his next of kin?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: No family history recorded. His sister, Claire, is listed as next of kin, with a phone number. He was living with her before the arrest. Funny thing: when I said her name this morning, he looked at me. Just for a second.

steps.label: Ask about work, home and the legal situation
steps.player: Tom, what do we know about his life before, and why he's here?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: Worked at a warehouse until last spring, then lived with his sister. The court found him not competent to stand trial and sent him for competency restoration. That's all the packet says about the charge.

steps.label: Ask about self-harm and aggression
steps.player: Elias, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or anyone else? ... Tom, any self-harm or aggression since he came in?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No response.

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: None here. He hasn't tried to hurt himself or anyone. He barely moves. The agitation the jail injected him for was before he went quiet.

steps.label: Ask for his vital signs
steps.player: Tom, what were his last observations?

beats.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
beats.text: At half seven: temperature thirty-seven point six, pulse one hundred and eight, blood pressure one forty-two over eighty-eight, breathing eighteen, oxygen ninety-eight percent on air. On arrival it was thirty-seven point two and ninety-six.

steps.label: Stand back and observe for a minute
steps.player: I'm just going to watch for a minute, Elias. You don't need to do anything.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: For a full minute he does not move. His gaze stays fixed and he blinks only twice. His hands lie in his lap exactly as they were.

steps.label: Take his pulse
steps.player: Elias, I'm going to hold your wrist to feel your pulse.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: Pulse about 110, regular. His skin is warm and slightly damp.

steps.label: Look at his mouth and hydration
steps.player: I'm going to look at your lips and mouth with this light, Elias.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: Lips cracked and the inside of his mouth is dry. He does not open his mouth when asked, but does not resist.

steps.label: Check his pupils
steps.player: Now I'll shine the light in each eye, briefly.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: Pupils equal and react to light. No nystagmus. He blinks at the light but his gaze returns to the wall.

steps.label: Scratch your head in an exaggerated way (imitation)
steps.player: Elias, watch me for a moment.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: He does not copy the movement.

steps.label: Lift his arm and let go (posturing)
steps.player: I'm going to lift your right arm, Elias, and then let it go.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: When you let go, his arm stays where you left it, at shoulder height, for over a minute, until you lower it.

steps.label: Bend and straighten his elbow (tone)
steps.player: Now I'll bend and straighten your elbow a few times.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: Slight, even resistance, like bending soft wax; the arm stays in each position you leave it. No lead-pipe rigidity and no cogwheeling.

steps.label: Stroke his palm (grasp reflex)
steps.player: I'm going to stroke the palm of your hand.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No grasp.

steps.label: Check his ankles for clonus
steps.player: Last thing, Elias. I'm going to flex each foot up quickly.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: No clonus at either ankle. Reflexes are normal.

fact_no_nonverbal_reply.text: No verbal or reliable nonverbal reply to questions (no nod, no hand squeeze). Pain cannot be documented as absent.

fact_onset.text: Withdrawn and staying in his cell for about a week, then stopped speaking four days before transfer.

fact_course.text: No one at Ashcroft has seen him speak or move normally.

fact_intake.text: Sips of water only when the cup is held to his lips; no food since arrival; about a quarter cup of fluid overnight.

fact_output.text: No urine charted since arrival; last voided yesterday afternoon per transport note. No bowel movement charted.

fact_sleep.text: Lay in one position from 03:00 to 07:00 without turning; eyes open at most checks. Sleep uncertain.

fact_haloperidol.text: Haloperidol 5 mg intramuscular twice, six and five days before transfer, for agitation. No regular medication since. No benzodiazepine given.

fact_allergies.reliability: jail record and admission sheet agree

fact_psych_history.text: One admission at 24 with psychosis; discharged on an antipsychotic, stopped within months. No previous episode like this recorded.

fact_medical_history.text: No medical history, seizures or head injury recorded. No blood tests in the packet.

fact_substances.text: Daily cannabis and weekend alcohol before arrest (self-report at jail intake); urine drug screen six weeks ago positive for cannabis only. In custody since.

fact_family.text: No family history recorded. Sister Claire is next of kin; he lived with her before the arrest.

fact_sister_glance.text: Briefly looked toward the sitter when his sister's name was said.

fact_social.text: Warehouse worker until last spring; living with his sister before arrest.

fact_legal.text: Found not competent to stand trial; transferred for competency restoration.

fact_risk_observed.text: No self-harm or aggression observed since arrival. Agitation treated at the jail preceded the mutism.

fact_risk_unassessable.text: Suicidal and violent thoughts could not be assessed: no reply. Not documented as absent.

fact_vitals_trend.text: 07:30: T 37.6 °C, HR 108, BP 142/88, RR 18, SpO2 98% on air. On arrival: T 37.2 °C, HR 96.

fact_no_echopraxia.text: No imitation of the examiner's movements.

orders.intro: Tell Tom and the charge nurse what you want done. Pick the orders, then give them. Each one is written to the EHR.

items.label: Vital signs with temperature every hour for now
items.feedback: His pulse and temperature are rising after recent haloperidol. Frequent observations catch autonomic instability early.

items.label: Fluid intake and output chart
items.feedback: Poor intake and no urine since yesterday afternoon: he needs his fluid balance measured, not estimated.

items.label: Bladder scan
items.feedback: No urine for many hours could be retention as well as dehydration.

items.label: Continue 1:1 observation
items.feedback: He cannot eat, drink or ask for help on his own. The sitter is also your best informant.

items.label: Pressure area care and repositioning
items.feedback: He did not turn over all night. Immobility brings pressure injury risk.

items.label: Creatine kinase (CK)
items.feedback: Needed with recent haloperidol, a rising temperature and pulse, and immobility: a raised CK supports neuroleptic malignant syndrome or muscle breakdown.

items.label: Basic metabolic panel (sodium, potassium, renal function, glucose)
items.feedback: Dehydration and poor intake: check sodium and kidney function.

items.label: Complete blood count
items.feedback: Infection and a raised white count belong in the differential of a rising temperature.

items.label: Liver function tests
items.feedback: Part of a medical workup for an altered mental state.

items.label: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
items.feedback: A treatable medical cause to exclude.

items.label: Urinalysis
items.feedback: Concentration and infection, once he passes urine.

items.label: Urine drug screen
items.feedback: Low yield after six weeks in custody, but reasonable in an unexplained change.

items.label: Lorazepam challenge, then re-examine
items.feedback: First-line for suspected catatonia, and a good response supports the diagnosis. Re-examine afterwards with the same steps.

items.label: Haloperidol for psychosis
items.feedback: Antipsychotics can worsen catatonia and precipitate neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and he already has a rising pulse and temperature after recent haloperidol. Hold antipsychotics until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

items.label: Olanzapine for psychosis
items.feedback: The same risk as any antipsychotic here: hold until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

items.label: Medical team review today
items.feedback: Rising pulse and temperature, dehydration and recent antipsychotic exposure need a medical assessment alongside yours.

items.label: Ask the medical team about clot prevention
items.feedback: Immobility in catatonia raises the risk of venous thromboembolism.

items.label: Call his sister for collateral history (with consent, or as policy allows)
items.feedback: She knows his baseline and the onset better than any packet.

items.label: Refer for ECT today
items.feedback: ECT is the treatment for catatonia that does not respond to lorazepam, or for malignant catatonia. Start with a lorazepam challenge and medical workup.

items.label: Record him as refusing to engage
items.feedback: Silence and stillness are signs to explain, not a choice to record. Keep investigating.

lab_results.bmp: Sodium 147 mmol/L (slightly raised), urea raised, creatinine at the upper limit of normal, potassium and glucose normal: consistent with dehydration.
lab_results.cbc: White cell count 11.2 (slightly raised); otherwise normal.

antipsychotic_hold.speaker: staff_bennett
antipsychotic_hold.text: Doctor, before I draw this up: his temperature's thirty-seven six, pulse a hundred and eight, and the packet says he had haloperidol last week. Do you want to hold it until the medical team has seen him?

choices.label: Hold it. Cancel the antipsychotic.
choices.reply: Thank you. I'll take it off.

choices.label: Give it as ordered.
choices.reply: I'm not comfortable giving it without the medical team's view. I'll document that I've held it and page them.
choices.chart_entry: Antipsychotic order held by nursing: safety concern raised with the prescriber; medical team paged.

call.speaker: staff_sitter_adler
call.text: Doctor? You'll want to come back and see him.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: His eyes move to you as you come in, and follow you to the chair.

steps.label: Offer him a drink
steps.player: Elias, would you like some water?

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: He takes the cup with both hands and drinks most of it.

steps.label: Lift his arm again
steps.player: I'm going to lift your arm again, Elias.

beats.speaker: pt_elias_ward
beats.shown: This time his arm comes back down to his lap when you let go.

lorazepam_reassessment.sitter_close: First thing he's said since he got here.
